Alex K: Heads-up — canary shows a ~12-18% p95 latency regression after we enabled layerwise FP8 calibration + partial quant. Not sure if it's calibration overhead, extra kernel switches, or KV cache thrash. Anyone seen this?

Priya S: Which canary/model and input profile? numbers? :thinking:

Alex K: Canary is gpt-smallish-v1 on dedicated canary pool (eu-west). Seq len 256 typical; p50 ~ same, p95 up ~18%. GPU SM util +6%, kernel launches per request up ~3x. Sampled logs look like a lot of tiny kernels and KV evict spam.

Alex K: Profiler snippet:
```
kernel_launches: 142 -> 412 per request
avg_kernel_time: 85us -> 27us (more launches)
kv_evictions: 0.6% -> 3.1% (seq>128 requests)
calib_step_ms: +220ms per cold-start
```

Jorge M: Calibration path likely triggering alternative kernels (slow pack/unpack or memcpy). Also dynamic switching between FP8 and int4 kernels per layer can cause thrash. Could be our kernel selector bouncing on per-layer metrics.

Mei L: We excluded lm_head but did we exclude embeddings? If embeddings got quantized/packed differently, KV blocks can change size/stride and increase eviction. Check quant_exclude list and the calibration sample size.

Alex K: Confirmed in config: `quant_exclude = ["lm_head"]` — embedding not excluded (my bad). Also calibration samples = 5k by default. Reducing to 1k reduced calibration time but didn't fully fix p95.

Priya S: Quick note: our int8 packing aligns to 256-byte tiles; when embeddings are quantized the KV tile count increases which fragments GPU memory and bumps eviction rate for long contexts. That maps to the kv_evictions jump.

Jorge M: Proposals: 1) Add embeddings to exclude list for the canary; 2) Limit kernel switches per request (e.g., prefer single FP8 fast-path unless sensitivity score > threshold); 3) Reduce calibration samples and do offline calibrations.

Mei L: Also ran a quick sensitivity probe: `./tools/quant-sensitivity --model gpt-smallish-v1 --samples 1500 --metric ppl` -> summary: middle layers (8-12) sensitivity ~0.07 (high), early layers ~0.01, last 2 layers ~0.03. If threshold is 0.02 we end up quantizing some sensitive midlayers. Suggest moving to per-layer threshold 0.04 or use top-k sensitive layer protection.

Alex K: Posted sensitivity output (summary):
```
layer 0-3: delta_ppl 0.009
layer 4-7: delta_ppl 0.018
layer 8-12: delta_ppl 0.071
layer 13-15: delta_ppl 0.026
lm_head: excluded
embeddings: quantized (delta_ppl 0.012)
```

Priya S: Interesting — that explains the quality vs perf trade. We should avoid quantizing 8-12 and exclude embeddings for now. Also patch kernel selector to prefer FP8 fused-kernels for attention + kv when seq>128. That reduces kernel count.

Jorge M: Kernel selector heuristic (proposal):
```
if seq_len > 128 and kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.85:
  prefer fused_fp8_attention_kernel
else if sensitivity(layer) < 0.04:
  allow int4 kernel
else:
  keep fp32/fp16
```
Cap switches_per_request = 1 (warmup allowed once).

Mei L: Measured kernel-switch cost in microbench: ~350us per switch (cold path) and ~120us warmed. Combined with extra memcpy it's enough to push p95. So cap is important.

Alex K: Action items:
- Priya: flip embeddings -> exclude on the canary and rerun (low effort).
- Jorge: prototype selector cap (1) + heuristic config PR.
- Mei: run sensitivity pass with 2k samples and produce recommended exclude list per model.
- I'll collect end-to-end traces (p95/p99 + kernel timeline) and attach.

Priya S: On it, will push canary change now and report in ~30m. :hammer:

runtime-bot: Deploy triggered for canary config update (canary/quant-exclude: embeddings) by Priya S.

infra-ci: Canary tests started — running perf-suite.

Alex K: Thanks team. If canary looks good we'll promote change and follow up with selector PR. :eyes:
